issues.body: Section 2.2 says the other `issue edit ... --body` call sites are the three listed ops-alert writers, after searching `scripts/**.py` and workflows. That is false in this checkout. Production call sites also exist in, among others, `scripts/metrics-alert.py`, `scripts/ledger-identity-watch.py`, `scripts/pat-validity.py`, `scripts/model-health.py`, `scripts/usage-alert.py`, `scripts/metrics.py`, `scripts/groom-alert.py`, `scripts/triage-stock-alert.py`, `scripts/groom-mint-alert.py`, `scripts/dispatch-stall-alert.py`, and `scripts/ci-latency-alert.py`. They may all target non-catalog issues, but the record neither enumerates nor proves that. This matters directly to the recommendation in section 5: a checkout-wide scan with the stated explicit allow-list of only the section 2.2 writers cannot pass on the current tree. Because the no-lock decision rests on `account-usage.py` being the sole catalog-body writer, an incomplete census leaves that premise unproved rather than merely imprecisely documented.
issues.fix_hint: Re-run and document a complete census of every production issue-body edit site, classify each target from independent routing evidence (labels/repository/issue selection), and update section 2.2 and the proposed test design accordingly. The invariant should be target-aware and should explicitly account for all current non-catalog writers; demonstrate that it passes the pristine tree and fails when a second catalog-targeting writer is introduced.
issues.title: The claimed exhaustive body-writer census omits many production writers

verdict.summary: The central conclusion that set-up-account does not edit existing account bodies is supported, but the record's supposedly exhaustive writer census is materially false. The repository contains many additional production `issue edit --body` call sites beyond the three listed, so the proposed exact allow-list test would reject the current tree and the document has not actually established its load-bearing single-writer premise with the claimed method. Correct the census and specify a target-aware invariant that accounts for every current writer before relying on it to WONTFIX the lock.
